title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is §2 ('the question of full faithfulness'), page 20, of the Longue Marche drafts. It is Grothendieck's formulation of the birational (field-theoretic) form of the anabelian conjecture.

The question. Let K, K' be fields of finite type over Q, with absolute Galois groups Π_K and Π_K', both fibred over Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q). Is every Π_Q-homomorphism Π_K' → Π_K induced by a field embedding, up to inner automorphisms? The next page adds the hypothesis that the image is open.

The reduction to a common constant field. Let k and k' be the algebraic closures of Q in K and K'. A Π_Q-homomorphism forces Γ_k' to map into a conjugate of Γ_k, so up to conjugation k ⊂ k' inside a fixed Q̄. Because k is algebraically closed in K, the tensor product K⊗_k k' is a field, and Π_{Kk'} = Π_K ×_{Γ_k} Γ_k'. So one may assume k = k' with the same image in Q̄.

The group extensions. Put Γ = Gal(Q̄/k). Then Π_K and Π_K' become extensions E_K, E_K' of Γ by the 'geometric' groups π_K = Gal(K̄/Kk̄) and π_K'. The question becomes: is every Γ-compatible (outer) homomorphism π_K' → π_K induced by a field embedding K ↪ K'?

The proposed strategy. To construct such an embedding one needs a recipe for reconstructing K and K' from E_K and E_K', i.e. from profinite outer groups with Γ-action. The next page suggests that Theorem 3 of the previous § (about P^1_K suitably punctured) might be the key. The heuristic is that the Γ-action is so 'draconian' that only geometric maps can commute with it, which uses arithmetic of the base field such as Q.

The problem served is the birational anabelian conjecture: a section of the Longue Marche in which the program of reconstructing function fields over number fields from their absolute Galois groups is set up.
errors: Direction slip: the question is first written as Π_K' → Π_K coming from a field homomorphism 'K' → K'. By contravariance it should come from K → K'. Grothendieck himself writes 'K ↪ K'' a few lines later.
The reduction 'k, k' isomorphic' is stated quickly. Strictly, one only gets k ⊂ k' up to conjugation, and then base-changes K to Kk'. This is standard and harmless.
The open-image hypothesis, which is necessary, is only added on the next page.

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of K ↦ Π_K on fields of finite type over Q, relative to Π_Q (Hom form with open image)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture: Esquisse 1984, letter to Faltings 1983). Proofs: Pop 1994/2000 (Isom form, absolute, finitely generated fields); Mochizuki 1999 (Hom form over sub-p-adic fields, function fields of arbitrary dimension)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche (circulated 1981)

ideas.what: Reduction to a common algebraically closed constant field, and reformulation via the extensions 1→π_K→Π_K→Γ→1 with outer Γ-action
ideas.modern_name: Geometric fundamental group with outer Galois action; relative (over k) anabelian setting
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche; letter to Faltings

ideas.what: Strategy of reconstructing K from E_K using results on punctured P^1 (the 'Th. 3' of the previous section)
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of function fields from Galois data, via curves/punctured lines
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche; not in Esquisse in this form

missed.claim: This is the original draft formulation of the birational anabelian Hom-conjecture. It already includes the reduction to a common constant field and the open-image proviso, and it identifies 'reconstructing K from the outer Γ-action' as the crux. All of this is known and has since been proved (Pop, Mochizuki). Nothing new beyond the historical record.
missed.quote: est-il vrai que tout Π_Q-homomorphisme Π_K' → Π_K provient d'un homomorphisme de corps
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historical: it documents the conjecture's original framing within the Longue Marche.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a well-known conjecture of Grothendieck, stated in Esquisse and the Faltings letter, and since proved by Pop and Mochizuki. The page is a draft formulation with a routine reduction step.
transcription_corrections: Line 5: the image indeed reads 'K' → K?'. This is Grothendieck's own direction slip, not a transcription error.
'disons un Γ_{Q̄/Q} —[?]' is uncertain; the word may be part of a parenthetical, and its meaning is unclear.
'donc[?] que E_K et E_K'' is more likely 'disons que E_K et E_K''.
'Pour construire un tel hom, en dernier[?], il faudrait' is perhaps 'Pour construire un tel hom, ou en deviner [l'existence], il faudrait'.
'[-est-][?] alors si' should read 'est alors si', with 'est' struck through.
